minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted 3-2 to keep Town Beach fees unchanged and reviewed Marshall Park schematic design and the cave.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the design consultant explain the schematic design schedule for Marshall Park, discussed the historic cave, and heard staff updates. It voted to hire the lifeguard slate and recommend a beach director, kept beach fees the same, and approved a shed, outfield banners and a wildlife-removal permission policy. Minutes for February were approved and March postponed.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted 3-2 to leave Town Beach fees the same as last year at all levels.
It voted to hire the slate of lifeguards and to recommend a beach director, pending confirmation of her water safety instructor status.
The commission voted 3-1 as heard to require its permission before planned trapping or removal of wildlife on park property.
It approved a youth-league shed at Powell field and outfield banners, the banners limited to Marshall Park and McNally field.
The facilities director is to arrange concrete core testing of the Marshall Park cave and report a timeline, after the design consultant presented the schematic design schedule.

why_it_matters: Beach day passes, seasonal passes and swim lessons stay at last year's rates for the 2023 season, while beach staffing ran over budget last year and was covered by moving money from a vacant salary line.
Marshall Park phase one may need a bond, with ARPA and grants hoped to close the gap, so residents could be asked to vote on borrowing; the cave testing result will bear on that design and cost.
watch_next: Facilities director's timeline for the cave core testing, due by the end of the following week.
Next meeting, May 10 or 17, timed to the Marshall Park design presentation; March minutes and the item on Adam Costa's email are still pending.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the lifeguard, beach director, fee, and policy-wording votes, but diverge on the banner amendment, the shed vote, the wildlife tally, and the attendee list. The official minutes are a summary and omit the shed vote, cave testing, and most budget figures, so the vote tallies and the banner scope need checking against the recording.
